I am rejecting the apartments response for the following reasons, based on California law (California Civil Code ******):


Failure to ******************************start="409" data-end="412"> According to California Civil Code ******, the landlord must provide an itemized statement and any remaining balance of the security deposit within 21 days after a tenant vacates the unit. I vacated the unit in June, yet I did not receive any itemized statement, PDF, or check within the 21-day period.


No Documentation or **********************start="763" data-end="766"> The apartment claims that a bill was generated and a check was issued, but I never received either. As evidence, I emailed both the apartment and the parent group on August 5th to inquire about the deposit, yet I still received no response and no documents.


Unjustified *******************start="1174" data-end="1177"> The apartment claims deductions of $125 for cleaning and $200 for another fee (Pent related). However:
I hired professional cleaners before moving out, and I have attached a video of the move-out condition of the unit to prove it was left in a clean condition.
No specific explanation or documentation for these charges has ever been provided. Under California law, any deduction must be clearly itemized and justified, and provided within 21 days. Since no proper notice or explanation was delivered within the statutory 21 days, the landlord forfeited the right to retain any portion of my deposit.

Failure to Return the **************************start="1863" data-end="1866"> Even if the landlord insists on claiming $325 in deductions (which I dispute), the remaining $1,200 refund shown on their own statement has never been sent to me. To this day, I have not received any check, any tracking information, or any response. This is a clear violation of California Civil Code ******.


Conclusion:
Because the apartment failed to comply with California law, did not provide timely notice, did not return the remaining $1,231.99 balance, and could not justify the $325 deductions, I request a full refund of my security deposit. Given that it has now been over two months since I vacated, their noncompliance is serious and unacceptable.

After further review of this matter, we found that the Statement of Deposit Accounting was prepared and the refund check was mailed within the required 21 days, in accordance with California Civil Code. However, it was discovered that the statement itself was not emailed to the resident as intended.
To ensure the resident is made whole and as a gesture of good faith, we are processing a full refund of the security deposit.
We apologize for the oversight in communication and have already taken steps to improve our internal process to prevent this from happening in the future.

items.text: Complaint Against:******************************************************************************************************** by Holland Partners Group Nature of Complaint:Failure to return the security deposit and prepaid rent for the rest of June in violation of California law; no response to the demand letter.Complaint Details:I am a former tenant of ************** Apartments, Unit 5221, managed by Holland Partners Group. I moved out on June 22, ******* addition to my security deposit, I also paid prepaid rent for the period after my move-out date, which the landlord is legally required to refund. Neither amount has been returned to **** sent a formal demand letter to the apartment management team and Holland Partners Group, referencing the amounts owed and citing California Civil Code ******. Despite this, I have not received any response or payment.California Civil Code ******(g)(1) requires landlords to return the security deposit, along with an itemized statement of any deductions, within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates. California Civil Code ******(l) further provides that if a landlord retains the security deposit in bad faith, the tenant may recover statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the deposit in addition to actual damages. In this case, nearly two months have passed since my move-out date, and my demand letter has gone unanswered.Desired Resolution:I am requesting:Immediate payment of my full security deposit of $1100 and my prepaid rent for the rest of June.

We take all resident concerns seriously and strive to resolve any disputes in a fair and timely manner.  We appreciate the opportunity to respond to Mr. ******** concerns and hope to work together toward a resolution. 

During Mr. ******** move out, our community was in the middle of a management transition. The property manager,sales associates, and maintenance manager were all onboarding a new team as they were transferring to a sister property. As the incoming property manager during that time, I was not directly involved in his original lease administration and was not aware of any domestic violence incidents or verbal agreements that may have predated my tenure.

With that said, I am more than happy to connect directly with Mr. ******* to review his account and any documentation he may have, so we can ensure everything is addressed thoroughly.

The earliest record we have regarding Mr. ******** move-out is an August ****** work order requesting a final walkthrough ahead of his lease ending on August 7, 2024. We were unable to locate a written 30-day notice to vacate,either from our current team, from former staff, or from Mr. ******* himself.

On August 21, 2024, our senior sales associate reached out to confirm his key return date and to ask if he had provided a written notice to any former team members. In his reply that same day, Mr. ******* stated:

My move out date was the 22nd of July. My lease ended on the 8th of August. I dropped off my keys on the 13th of August.

Under the lease agreement, move-out is considered the date the unit is surrendered and keys are returned, not the date personal belongings are removed. Based on Mr. ******** confirmation that keys were returned on August 13, 2024, and without a verified written notice to vacate date, our accounting team applied the standard lease requirement of 30 days rent responsibility from that date, resulting in charges through September 13, 2024.

I truly believe that had we connected sooner, we may have been able to resolve this matter much earlier. We remain open to reviewing any additional documentation Mr. ******* can provide, including written notice or paperwork related to California Civil Code ******. If such documentation is furnished,we will gladly reassess the account in accordance with California law.

Our goal is to resolve this in a way that is fair, and we welcome the opportunity to speak with Mr. ******* directly so we can work toward that outcome together.

Thank you for reaching out and providing details about your concerns. We appreciate the care you took in maintaining the unit during your residency. However, I would like to clarify that the charges you mentioned are in line with the standard policies and fees applied to all residents upon move-out.


The cleaning fee is reflective of the professional cleaning services required to ensure the unit is ready for the next tenant. This fee is assessed based on the condition of the apartment at the time of inspection, and while we acknowledge your efforts to keep the space clean, the full fee was necessary to bring the apartment up to our move-in standards.


Similarly, for painting and damages covers standard repainting after a year of tenancy. This charge is typical even in cases where there may not be visible damages, as paint tends to wear naturally over time. Additionally, any pre-existing conditions, such as the floor polish issue, should have been reported at move-in, and without prior documentation, we are unable to adjust the charge.


That said, we are happy to review the final statement and make any necessary adjustments if an error is found. However, as of now, the charges applied are standard and in accordance with your lease agreement. We encourage you to reach out if you have further questions or documentation regarding any issues present at move-in.
